title: Once the MFCC front end is counted, does the energy-optimal keyword model change?
lede: joining accel-cascade's committed results with accel-frontend's 46.8 nJ per frame: cascades' classifier-only saving of up to 28% becomes at most 0.42% of whole-system energy, while the most accurate model (about 0.75 test accuracy) costs 23 to 26 times the cheapest classifier but only 5% more system energy (modelled, not measured)
summary: accel-cascade found two-stage cascades cut classifier energy by up to 28% but said the saving would vanish next to the MFCC front end. This project computes it by joining that project's committed per-design energies and accuracies (5 seeds, 40 models each) with accel-frontend's 46.77 nJ per frame, at 50 frames and 4 decisions per second (584.6 nJ per decision). The cascades' whole-system saving is at most 0.42% (mean over seeds, accuracy targets 0.50 to 0.74), with 0.3 to 1.4 points of test accuracy lost; the front end must get about 10 to 30 times cheaper before cascades reach a few per cent, and 100 times cheaper for up to 17%. In the other direction, the model with the best validation accuracy (test 0.747 to 0.758) draws 23 to 26 times the cheapest model above 0.5 validation accuracy (test 0.47 to 0.49) in the classifier, but only 5.2 to 5.8% more in the whole system. Modelled energy from accel-kws constants (checked against Horowitz 2014 within 4% in accel-horowitzcheck); the front-end scale factors are a sweep; accuracies are from float features, not the integer front end; nothing is retrained or measured.
